messages.subject: NUSE plots on hapmap 250K chips
parts:
Dear all,

first of all congratulations on the great work you are doing. It is
very impressive indeed.

I have been analyzing the quality of some affy snp 250K chips and when
creating the corresponding NUSE plots I noticed that the distributions
of the standard errors was quite different to the ones usually
observed using affy expression arrays. A pdf containing NUSE values
for the 48 hapmap samples on both Nsp and Sty can be found here:
<http://pierotti.group.ifom-ieo-campus.it/jreid/hapmap,NUSE.pdf>
As you can see most medians are very close to 1 which should indicate
good quality hybs but then what I don't understand is the skewness of
the data with the lower hinges also lying around one. I don't think it
has anything to do with the implementation of plotNUSE because it is
compatible with the one provided in affyPLM (apart from the default
boxplot behaviour, which has range set to 0 in affyPLM).
Does anyone know why this could be, is it a peculiarity of these kind
of chips (which I have just starting using...)

Many thanks,
J.

Details:
I am running the latest version of the package to my knowledge
(0.9.2), here is my sessionInfo and the code for generating the above
mentioned pdf.

## start code
library(aroma.affymetrix)

dataSetName <- "hapmap"
chipTypes <- c("Mapping250K_Nsp", "Mapping250K_Sty")

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)

qamList <- list()

for (chipType in chipTypes) {
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(dataSetName, chipType=chipType)
plm <- RmaPlm(cs)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
qamList[[chipType]] <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
}

pdf(file=sprintf("%s,NUSE.pdf", dataSetName))
for (i in 1:length(chipTypes)) {
plotNuse(qamList[[i]], main=sprintf("NUSE (%s)", chipTypes[i]))
}
dev.off()

## end code
